_about: Single source of truth for every rendering, and the auditable term ledger (check 5). ONE rendering per referent for the whole book. status per entry: 'attested' (form used in English scholarship), 'provisional' (romanization mine), 'decided' (a project style call). Flag the book's main cast with principal:true (optional cast one-liner, cast_order). Sections render as glossary headings; keys starting with '_' are ignored.

周恩来.cast: Director of the Party's underground work in Shanghai and founder of the Central Special Branch (1898–1976).
周恩来.note: Conventional pinyin; the Party's intelligence chief in this period and the author's ultimate superior.

顾顺章.cast: The Party's first intelligence chief, a stage magician; defected to the Kuomintang in 1931 (1903–1935).
顾顺章.note: Head of the Central Special Branch whose 1931 defection wrecked the Shanghai underground.

陈赓.cast: Head of the Special Branch's intelligence section, under the alias Wang Yong; later a PLA general (1903–1961).
陈赓.note: Whampoa first class; saved Chiang Kai-shek's life in 1925; ran the Second (intelligence) Section.

王庸.note: Chen Geng's cover name in Shanghai ("Mr. Wang").

蒋介石.cast: Leader of the Kuomintang and its government; the Party's chief adversary (1887–1975).

董健吾.note: The "Red Pastor": an Anglican clergyman and Communist agent who ran St. Peter's Church as a safe house.

徐恩曾.note: Chief of the Kuomintang's civilian secret service, the Zhongtong.

李强.note: Built the Party's first secret radio; a principal source on the Special Branch's origins.

杨度.note: Monarchist theorist turned secret Communist agent (1875–1931).

梅宝玑.note: Honored as the Party's first intelligence source (1881–1947).

梅龚彬.note: Long-buried Communist agent inside the Kuomintang; Mei Baoji's nephew (1901–1975).

潘汉年.note: Chen Geng's successor in intelligence work; jailed in the 1955 case that bears his name.

张慧冲.note: Film star and founder of "Shanghai-style magic," admired by Gu Shunzhang.

李维汉.note: Senior Party leader; on the Standing Committee that founded the Special Branch.

瞿秋白.note: Party leader after August 1927; writer; executed 1935.

胡鄂公.note: 1911 revolutionary and early Marxist who introduced Chen Geng to Yang Du.

徐梅坤.note: First head of the Jiangsu committee's "dog-beating squad," the Special Branch's forerunner.

宗孟平.note: Communist organizer of the Yixing rising (1927) and later an underground intelligence agent; an obscure figure known chiefly from Party memoirs.

匡亚明.note: Yixing-area Communist organizer; after 1949 a noted educator and president of Nanjing University (1906–1996).

史砚芬.note: Yixing revolutionary and martyr, executed at Yuhuatai in 1928 aged 25; not the same person as Shi Yaobin.

陈云.note: Young Jiangsu labor organizer who briefly ran the Central Special Branch after Gu's defection; later the chief economic planner of the People's Republic (1905–1995).

陈独秀.note: Co-founder and first general secretary of the Chinese Communist Party; blamed for the 1927 defeat and later expelled (1879–1942).

彭述之.note: Party propaganda chief and Chen Duxiu ally who followed him into the Trotskyist opposition (1895–1983).

罗亦农.note: A leader of the Shanghai workers' uprisings; captured and executed in 1928 (1902–1928).

赵世炎.note: A leader of the Shanghai workers' uprisings; executed in 1927 (1901–1927).

汪寿华.note: Head of the Shanghai General Labor Union; strangled by Green Gang gangsters on the eve of the April 12, 1927 coup (1899–1927).

蔡孟坚.note: Kuomintang intelligence officer in Wuhan who arrested Gu Shunzhang in 1931 (1905–2001).

薛岳.note: Northern Expedition commander at Shanghai in 1927, later a leading Nationalist general (1896–1998).

杨之华.note: Leading woman organizer of the Party and wife of Qu Qiubai; wrote of Gu Shunzhang under the pen name Du Ning (1901–1973).

李哲时.note: Luo Yinong's wife; later known as Li Wenyi, whose memoir is a source here (1901–?).

李文宜.note: The later name of Li Zheshi, Luo Yinong's widow.

贺稚华.note: The traitor of this chapter; the standard scholarship writes her name He Zhihua with a different second character (贺治华).

何家兴.note: He Zhihua's husband, killed with her in the 1928 reprisal.

郑超麟.note: Editor of Bolshevik and a leading memoirist of the early Party (1901–1998).

苏兆征.note: Seamen's-union leader and early Party figure (1885–1929).

朱德.note: Later commander-in-chief of the Red Army and the PLA; He Zhihua was his wife (1886–1976).

朱敏.note: Zhu De's daughter by He Zhihua (1926–2009).

邓小平.note: Then a young member of the Central Secretariat; later China's paramount leader (1904–1997).

邓颖超.note: Zhou Enlai's wife and a Women's Commission leader (1904–1992).

陈延年.note: Chen Duxiu's eldest son; arrested and killed 1927.

夏明翰.note: Communist martyr executed 1928; the source prints his given name with a variant character.

叶挺.note: Commander of the Nanchang Uprising forces (1896–1946).

张国焘.note: A founder of the Party; his memoirs are a source (1897–1979).

张作霖.note: The Fengtian warlord who then held Beijing (1875–1928).

康生.note: Then a Shanghai underground cadre; later the Party's security chief (1898–1975).

杨登瀛.note: Alias Bao Junfu; the Party's first double agent inside the enemy services.

鲍君甫.note: The cover name of Yang Dengying.

钱大钧.note: Commander of the Songhu Garrison who signed Luo Yinong's execution order (1893–1982).

张太雷.note: Communist leader killed in the 1927 Canton Uprising; his widow was Wang Yizhi.

汪精卫.note: Kuomintang leader; later head of the Japanese-sponsored regime (1883–1944).

胡锦涛.note: General Secretary of the Communist Party and President of China, 2002–2012/13.

穆欣.note: Former editor-in-chief of Guangming Daily and biographer of Chen Geng.

彭湃.note: Peasant-movement leader (1896–1929), "king of the peasant movement," founder of the Hailufeng Soviet; CCP Politburo member, arrested at Jingyuanli and executed at Longhua, 1929.

杨殷.note: CCP Central Military Commission head (1892–1929); a leader of the 1927 Guangzhou Uprising; executed with Peng Pai at Longhua.

颜昌颐.note: CCP military cadre (1898–1929), arrested and executed with Peng Pai and Yang Yin.

邢士贞.note: Jiangsu provincial Military Commission cadre for soldiers’ work; executed with Peng Pai, 1929.

白鑫.note: CCP Central Military Commission secretary (1903–1929) who betrayed the Jingyuanli meeting to the Kuomintang; killed by the Red Squad on Avenue Joffre, 11 Nov 1929.

张际春.note: Deputy commander of the Shanghai General Labor Union pickets; the fifth man arrested at Jingyuanli (he survived).

范争波.note: Kuomintang Shanghai party-headquarters official and police inspector who ran Bai Xin; wounded in the Red Squad ambush.

范争洛.note: Fan Zhengbo’s brother, wounded in the same ambush.

安娥.note: Poet and lyricist (1905–1976), born Zhang Shiyuan; the Party planted her as Yang Dengying’s secretary. Later wrote "The Newsboy’s Song" with Nie Er and married the playwright Tian Han.

连德生.note: CCP member placed as Yang Dengying’s bodyguard and courier.

柯麟.note: Communist physician (1901–1991), alias Ke Dawen; ran the Dasheng Hospital as a Party front; later the long-serving director of the Kiang Wu Hospital in Macau.

贺诚.note: Communist physician (1901–1992), alias He Yusheng; Ke Lin’s partner at the Dasheng Hospital, later head of the PLA medical service.

李一氓.note: Communist writer and cadre (1903–1990) who worked with the Special Branch in Shanghai.

杨剑虹.note: Green Gang man and early Kuomintang investigator who recruited Yang Dengying; driven to suicide in 1928.

陈立夫.note: Kuomintang organizer (1900–2001); with his brother Chen Guofu, head of the "CC Clique" and its intelligence apparatus (the Zhongtong).

陈果夫.note: Kuomintang power-broker (1892–1951), elder of the two Chen brothers of the "CC Clique."

张道藩.note: Kuomintang official and propagandist (1897–1968) involved in setting up the party’s Shanghai intelligence work.

赵子柏.note: Interpreter and detective-chief at the French Concession police, an informant of Dong Jianwu’s.

黄金荣.note: Boss of the Green Gang (1868–1953) and a detective in the French Concession police; the pre-eminent gangster of old Shanghai.

罗青长.note: Veteran Party intelligence officer (1918–2014), later head of the Central Investigation Department and of Taiwan work; the last official Zhou Enlai received.

欧阳新.note: Special Branch contact to whom Dong Jianwu telephoned the timing of the police in the Bai Xin operation.

蔡飞.note: Red Squad member in the Bai Xin operation.

邵达夫.note: Red Squad member in the Bai Xin operation.

谭忠余.note: Red Squad gunman (also in the ch. 1 roster); took part in the Bai Xin killing.

胡兰波.note: Red Squad gunman in the Bai Xin operation.

罗登贤.note: CCP labor leader (1905–1933); named to the reconstituted Jiangsu Provincial Standing Committee in 1929.

徐锡根.note: CCP labor cadre named to the 1929 Jiangsu Provincial Standing Committee.

赵容.note: The real name of Kang Sheng, then on the Jiangsu Provincial Standing Committee.

陈建宇.note: Author of "The Legend of Chen Yangshan, Lucky General of the Hidden Front" (2006); Chen Yangshan’s son.

王光远.note: Author of "The Red Pastor Dong Jianwu" (2001) and other Party-history works.

张国栋.note: Former Zhongtong insider whose memoir describes the Kuomintang Investigation Section.

紫丁.note: Author of the "Biography of Li Qiang" (2004).

李关德.note: Author of "Jing’an by the Sea" (2003), a local history of the Jing’an district.

范梦菊.note: Proprietor of the Sanmin Photo Studio, a Special Branch weapons cache; brought the guns up for the Fenglin Bridge rescue.

李延明.note: Li Qiang’s son, a scholar of political theory.

周军.note: Co-author of "Yang Dengying: The Special Figure Zhou Enlai Never Ceased to Think Of" (2001).

潘莹斌.note: Co-author of the same Yang Dengying biography.

力平.note: Author of "The Life of Zhou Enlai" (2001).

张佐良.note: Zhou Enlai’s personal physician for his last decade and author of a memoir (1997).

鞠书章.note: Cadre named in Li Qiang’s 1968–69 diary.

李辅仁.note: Cadre named in Li Qiang’s diary.

徐元奎.note: Cadre named in Li Qiang’s diary.

李班.note: Person named in Li Qiang’s diary.

罗可群.note: Co-author of a 1981 study of Peng Pai.

熊瑾玎.note: The “Red Boss”; managed the underground Party's Shanghai finances from 1928 and kept the Yunnan Road safe house with Zhu Duanshou (1886–1973).

朱端绶.note: Xiong Jinding's wife in a marriage that began as underground cover; guarded the Politburo's secret premises (1908–1994).

熊畅苏.note: Daughter of Xiong Jinding and Zhu Duanshou; the chapter's chief living witness.

龚饮冰.note: Xiong Jinding's predecessor as the Centre's chief accountant; a lifelong underground financier (1900–1976).

龚育之.note: Gong Yinbing's son; Party historian and theorist (1929–2007).

熊笑三.note: Nationalist general and Xiong Jinding's estranged son.

南汉宸.note: First governor of the People's Bank of China; CCPIT chairman (1895–1967).

洪扬生.note: Chief of the First (General Affairs) Section of the Central Special Branch.

吴阶平.note: Eminent urologist who attended the Party leadership (1917–2011).

王勃.note: Early Tang poet, author of the “Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng” (c. 650–676).

白居易.note: One of the great Tang poets (772–846).

刘少奇.note: Senior Party leader; head of state, purged and died in the Cultural Revolution (1898–1969).

博古.note: Party name of Qin Bangxian, a leader of the Moscow-trained group (1907–1946).

凯丰.note: Party name of He Kequan, propaganda leader (1906–1955).

向忠发.note: Party general secretary 1928–31; captured and shot after Gu Shunzhang's defection (1880–1931).

李立三.note: Party leader who gave his name to the “Li Lisan line” of 1930 (1899–1967).

贺龙.note: Founder of the West Hunan–Hubei Soviet; later a PLA marshal (1896–1969).

毛泽东.note: Leader of the CCP and the People's Republic (1893–1976).

熊耕午.note: Eldest daughter of Xiong Jinding and Zhu Duanshou (d. 1961).

耕午.note: Eldest daughter of Xiong Jinding and Zhu Duanshou (d. 1961).

骊午.note: Fifth child; died young of diphtheria.

中央特科.note: The CCP's first intelligence and security service (1927–1935), Shanghai. English form per Wikipedia.

红队.note: The Special Branch's Action (Third) Section, its assassination unit; also "the dog-beating squad."

国民党.note: Rendered "Kuomintang" throughout, the conventional English name.

南洋兄弟烟草公司.note: The largest Chinese-owned tobacco firm, rival to British-American Tobacco; Gu Shunzhang was a foreman at its Shanghai works.

上海市总工会.note: The Communist-led federation of the city's unions, organizing force of the three workers' uprisings.

组织局.note: The Party Center's coordinating body over its organization, propaganda, and secretariat organs, set up November 1927.

东方大学.en: the University of the Toilers of the East
东方大学.pinyin: the University of the Toilers of the East
东方大学.note: The Communist University of the Toilers of the East (KUTV) in Moscow, which trained Asian revolutionaries.

青洪帮.note: The two great Shanghai secret societies.

中统.note: Shorthand for the Kuomintang’s civilian intelligence service (in full, from 1938, the Central Bureau of Investigation and Statistics), grown out of the Central Organization Department’s Investigation Section.

调查科.note: The Kuomintang Central Organization Department’s Party Affairs Investigation Section, the seed of the Zhongtong.

淞沪警备司令部.note: The Kuomintang garrison authority for the Shanghai–Woosung area, with its headquarters and execution ground at Longhua.

中央军委.note: The CCP’s central body directing military and soldiers’ work.

达生医院.note: A clinic run by the Communist doctors Ke Lin and He Cheng as a secret Party organ.

圣彼得堂.note: The Anglican church on Avenue Road where Dong Jianwu was presiding pastor and ran a Party liaison post.

怀恩堂.note: A Baptist church on Seymour Road, distinct from St. Peter’s though sometimes confused with it.

支部生活.note: Internal bulletin of the central-organs branch, edited by Deng Yingchao.

上海.note: Seat of the Party Center and its underground in this period.

龙华.note: Site of the Songhu Garrison headquarters and its execution ground, on Shanghai's southern edge.

蒲石路.note: A street of the French Concession, today's Changle Road.

静安寺路.note: A main Settlement road past Jing'an Temple, today's Nanjing West Road.

经远里.note: The lane on Xinzha Road where Peng Pai and the others were arrested on 24 Aug 1929.

新闸路.note: Shanghai street in the International Settlement; the scene of the Jingyuanli arrests.

霞飞路.note: The great French Concession boulevard (today Huaihai Middle Road); the "Avenue Joffre" of the chapter title.

枫林桥.note: A road fork near Longhua where the Special Branch tried and failed to ambush the prison van.

秦城监狱.note: The high-security prison near Beijing where Yang Dengying was held, 1968–69, ostensibly for his protection.

和合坊.note: The Avenue Joffre lane where Bai Xin was killed.

卡德路.note: French Concession street (today Shimen No. 2 Road).

爱文义路.note: International Settlement street (today Beijing West Road).

嵩山路.note: French Concession street with the police station watched in the Bai Xin operation.

云南路.note: Shanghai; today Yunnan Middle Road. No. 447 held the Fuxing safe house.

福州路.note: Shanghai; the old Fourth Horse Road (Sima Road).

天蟾舞台.note: Famous Peking-opera theater on Fourth Horse Road; today the Labor Theater.

生黎医院.note: The clinic downstairs from the Fuxing safe house.

湘鄂西.note: He Long's soviet base area around Honghu (Xiang–E–Xi).

洪湖.note: Lake district of the West Hunan–Hubei Soviet.

康悌路.note: French Concession street; French name uncertain, kept as pinyin.

西门路.note: French Concession street; today Zizhong Road.

慎成里.note: A lane compound in the French Concession.

马斯南路.note: French Concession; today Sinan Road, site of the 1946 Zhou Residence.

跑马厅.note: The Shanghai Race Club grounds; today People's Park and Square.

陶乐春.note: A Sichuan restaurant on Fourth Horse Road.

晋察冀.note: The Jin–Cha–Ji border region, a base area in the war years.

打狗队.note: Special Branch slang for the assassination squad that eliminated traitors; "beating the dogs" (dagou).

亭子间.note: The small, cheap back room over the kitchen stair in a Shanghai lane house; a byword for the poor lodging of writers and radicals.

二房东.note: A middleman who leased a whole dwelling and sublet it in parts.

白色恐怖.note: The Kuomintang's campaign of arrests and executions against Communists from 1927.

哈同花园.note: The vast estate (Aili Garden) of the Baghdadi-Jewish magnate Silas Aaron Hardoon.

老虎灶.note: An old-Shanghai shop selling boiled water, its stove shaped like a crouching tiger.

拆白党.note: Shanghai swindlers who fleeced women through false courtship.

会审公廨.note: The concession court with mixed foreign and Chinese jurisdiction.

湘绣.note: Hunan embroidery, one of China's four great embroidery traditions.

石库门.note: The stone-framed-gate lane house typical of old Shanghai.

驳壳枪.note: The Mauser C96 "box cannon" pistol, the standard sidearm of the Red Squad.

国际歌.note: The socialist anthem, sung by the condemned prisoners at Longhua.

福兴字号.note: The shop-name cover for the Yunnan Road safe house (also written 福兴商号).

抄靶子.note: Shanghai slang for the concession police's snap street body-searches.

明矾水.note: Alum solution used as a developer for invisible ink.

红烧狮子头.note: Large red-cooked pork meatballs, a Huaiyang dish.

伍豪.note: Zhou Enlai's best-known underground cover name.

十里洋场.note: Stock epithet for Shanghai's foreign concessions.

四人帮.note: Jiang Qing, Zhang Chunqiao, Yao Wenyuan, and Wang Hongwen.

词牌.note: The named metrical pattern of a classical ci lyric.
